button.intent: A control that performs an action. Navigation is an anchor and is governed elsewhere.
button.namespaceNote: Bulma has no per-component prefix — `.button` composes with generic `is-*` modifiers that other components also use. So the namespace lists the modifiers that change a button's appearance, plus this product's own `cp-btn-` prefix. Naming them explicitly is the cost of a library that shares one modifier vocabulary across components; the alternative, matching all of `is-*`, would claim classes belonging to columns and tags.

small.intent: Terminal-dense surfaces: log rows, inline filters.

large.reason: Emphasis is what the pattern name carries. Size as a second emphasis channel means two ways to say the same thing, which eventually disagree.

primary.intent: The one action a screen most wants. At most one per view.
primary.notes: Promoted first: this product draws a neon edge that Bulma has no modifier for, which is a STRUCTURAL divergence rather than a colour change. That is one of the three promotion triggers.

secondary.intent: A supporting action beside a primary one. Outlined, so it reads as available without competing.
secondary.notes: Promoted because the call site composed three classes. Counting classes is a decent proxy for 'this is a concept, not a combination'.

destructive.intent: An action that cannot be undone easily. Filled, because the weight IS the warning.

ghost.intent: A borderless action inside an already-dense panel: dismiss, collapse, toggle a pane.
ghost.notes: ALLOWED here and FORBIDDEN in the Hot Tone example, on purpose. The risk is identical — a borderless control reads as text — but this product's surfaces are dark panels with visible chrome, so the affordance survives. Two products reaching opposite conclusions from the same trade-off is the normal case, and it is why this decision belongs to the product rather than to the tool.

success.reason: Green means 'the system did the thing'. A button is a request, not a result. Reserving green for confirmation keeps it meaningful.

warning.reason: Feedback, not intent. An action worth hesitating over is destructive, and that pattern exists.

info.reason: In this palette cyan IS the primary hue, so an info button is a primary button that does not behave like one.

neutral.intent: A button coloured by an absolute palette name.
neutral.reason: `is-light`, `is-dark`, `is-white` and `is-black` are fixed palette entries. In Bulma they are also variant MODIFIERS whose absolute lightness other components depend on, so they cannot follow a theme even in principle.

text.reason: Indistinguishable from a link, and this product already has `ghost` for a low-emphasis action. Two patterns for one job is how a vocabulary starts growing without anyone deciding to.
